lessons.title: Build ladder: phase to COT
lessons.physicalIntuition: Validate energy flow first, then add pulse decisions one mechanism at a time so a failure has a small search space.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Gate progression on conversion ratio, state slopes, volt-second/charge balance, nonideal voltage drops, one-shot timing, ripple crossings, and current-limit overshoot bounds.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Each rung has its own testbench and preserved parameter set. A failed invariant blocks the next rung.
lessons.transferQuestion: Which test proves the one-shot works independently of the buck phase?

lessons.title: Scale to two and N phases
lessons.physicalIntuition: Scaling duplicates physical states but introduces coordination and coupled-loop behavior that a single phase cannot reveal.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Generalize the capacitor equation to sum N phase currents, define scheduler invariants and fairness, then add balance and shedding states with explicit bandwidth/hysteresis.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Generate or instantiate phases with per-phase parameter arrays; never use one shared current state. N-phase symmetry is a test case, not a hard-coded result.
assumptions: scheduler and balance loops are disclosed educational choices
lessons.transferQuestion: Which result should remain invariant when identical phases are permuted, and which scheduler trace may change?

lessons.title: Timing nonidealities, mismatch, startup, and transients
lessons.physicalIntuition: Realistic delay and mismatch reveal whether the architecture depends on perfect simultaneity, perfect sensing, or impossible initial conditions.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Bound expected delay-induced current overshoot, calculate symmetry-breaking trends from L/DCR/sense mismatch, and use energy/charge bounds for startup and load-step sanity checks.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Run deterministic scenario matrices with explicit initial conditions and seeds. Record actual event times, denied pulses, current limits, phase currents, and output recovery.
lessons.transferQuestion: Which mismatch produces equal sensed currents but unequal actual thermal stress?

lessons.title: Validation, adversarial review, and explanation
lessons.physicalIntuition: Validation asks independent questions that a wrong model is unlikely to answer consistently. Tool execution proves execution, not physical truth; analytical agreement proves only the tested relationship.
lessons.mathematicalDerivation: Check conversion, state slopes, volt-second/charge residuals, boundary behavior, summed-current identity, ideal interleaving, symmetry, and mismatch direction. Compare step/time tolerance sensitivity and preserve tool/version logs.
lessons.modelingConsequence: Classify each file as syntax-reviewed, alternative-engine cross-checked, or executed in target PSpice. Explain every block's purpose, abstraction, and excluded behavior before sign-off.
assumptions: no claim exceeds the recorded evidence
lessons.interaction: Adversarial technical review and oral defense
lessons.transferQuestion: A waveform matches expected Vo but violates charge balance. Which result do you trust and what do you inspect next?
